title: Breach: Genesis Tree, Splinters and the Path to Xesht
summary: How Breach works in Path of Exile 2 from a normal map encounter through the Breach Hive, Genesis Tree, Stronghold and the Xesht pinnacle boss, including Splinters, Wombgift crafting and Atlas points.
description: A reference for the Breach end-game system in Path of Exile 2: recognising Breaches on the Atlas, the encounter timer, Hive vs normal Breach, Splinters and Breachstones, the Genesis Tree, Wombgift crafting, Stronghold progression and how to reach Xesht.
prerequisites: Maps unlocked and you can sustain Waystones
A character that can clear a normal Breach without dying
Some Splinters banked from early Breach encounters
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Xesht, We That Are One, the Breach pinnacle boss of Path of Exile 2

items.title: What is a Breach on the Atlas?
body: A Breach is an end-game map encounter marked by Clasped Hands. Entering it opens a breach that spills monsters; killing them before the breach closes banks Splinters.
Splinters of the same Breachlord combine into a Breachstone, which is the key to deeper Breach content.

items.title: Why does my Breach end so fast?
body: Every Breach has an encounter timer. Killing monsters inside extends the breach, while idle time drains it. Closed or small maps end faster than open layouts.

items.title: What is the Breach Hive?
body: The Breach Hive is the upgraded, self-contained version of the Breach system. It trades the open-map scramble for a focused lane with its own objectives and better rewards.

items.title: How do I reach Xesht?
body: Xesht, We That Are One, is the Breach pinnacle boss. You reach it by progressing the Breach questline through Breachstones, the Hive and the Stronghold until the pinnacle invitation opens.

sections.title: Recognising a Breach on the Atlas
paragraphs: Breaches appear as Clasped Hands nodes on the Atlas. Hovering shows the Breachlord and the tier, which scales the monster level and reward density.
Running a map that contains a Breach spawns the hands in the zone. Walking into them begins the encounter immediately, so clear your approach first if your build is fragile.
Each Breachlord has its own Splinter type. Keep Splinters sorted by Breachlord; mixing them does not combine into a usable Breachstone.
bullets: Clasped Hands = Breach node on the Atlas
Tier scales monster level and rewards

sections.title: The encounter timer
paragraphs: When the breach opens, a timer starts. Killing monsters inside the breach refills the timer and spawns more, so a fast, mobile character sustains the breach longer.
Clasped Hands drop inside the breach. Always collect them before the breach collapses; uncollected hands are lost when the timer ends.
Map layout matters: open maps let you chain packs and keep the timer alive, while narrow maps force backtracking and cut the run short.
bullets: Open maps sustain Breaches better than closed maps

sections.title: Unstable Breach vs the Breach Hive
paragraphs: A normal Breach is a timed, open-map scramble for Splinters. You race the clock and the map to grab as many Clasped Hands as possible.
The Breach Hive is the higher tier: a self-contained Breach space with dedicated objectives. It drops denser rewards and feeds the Genesis Tree and Stronghold progress.
Spend normal Breaches farming Splinters and Breachstones; move into the Hive once you want Genesis points and the pinnacle path rather than raw Splinter volume.
bullets: Breach Hive = objectives, Genesis points, better rewards
Hive assumes a stronger, faster character

sections.title: Rewards and Splinters
paragraphs: Breach Splinters combine into a Breachstone for the matching Breachlord. Breachstones are the repeatable key to the Hive and deeper content.
Wombgift is a special Breach reward currency used for Breach-themed jewellery crafting, such as special rings, amulets and belts.
Catalysts, Breach Rings and other Breach-themed items drop from Breach content and feed either your character or the trade economy; the trade guide covers pricing them.
bullets: Breach items feed trade or self-use

sections.title: Genesis Tree planner
paragraphs: The Genesis Tree is the Breach passive tree. It is organised into four quadrants, each tied to a Breachlord theme and the rewards that Breachlord emphasises.
Spend Genesis points on the quadrant that matches what you farm most: Splinter yield, Hive rewards, Wombgift chance, or pinnacle preparation. Spreading too early dilutes the benefit.
Re-spec is possible, so commit to one quadrant per character until you have enough points to branch out. Confirm point costs on the live tree before allocating.
bullets: Four quadrants, one per Breachlord theme
Point costs shown on the live tree

sections.title: Wombgift crafting
paragraphs: Wombgift is the Breach currency used to craft special Breach-themed jewellery, such as rings, amulets and belts with Breach-flavoured modifiers.
Decide what you want before spending: a specific slot (ring vs amulet vs belt) and the modifier direction. Wombgift is scarce early, so target one item rather than sampling all three.
If you mainly trade, bank Wombgifts and sell them; the currency-exchange guide covers turning them into liquid currency efficiently.
bullets: Bank and trade if you do not self-craft

sections.title: Stronghold progression
paragraphs: The Breach Stronghold is the quest milestone that bridges the Hive and the pinnacle boss. Completing it is what opens the path to Xesht.
Prioritise the Stronghold objective over farming extra Splinters once it is available; the pinnacle invitation is worth more than marginal Splinter volume.
Treat the Stronghold like a boss gate: arrive with your defensive board intact, because the objective assumes a character that already clears Hives comfortably.
bullets: Finish it before farming more Splinters

sections.title: Reaching Xesht
paragraphs: Xesht, We That Are One, is the Breach pinnacle boss. The invitation opens after the Stronghold step of the Breach questline is complete.
Xesht has its own fight mechanics; this guide covers the path and preparation, while the boss page covers its attacks and phases in detail.
Only attempt Xesht once your character clears Hives without issue, since the pinnacle assumes a fully geared Breach runner.

cards.title: Open maps win Breaches
body: Players consistently report that open, fast-clearing maps sustain the breach timer far better than narrow layouts.

cards.title: One quadrant at a time
body: Spreading Genesis points across all four quadrants early is the most common regret among Breach farmers.

cards.title: Stronghold before farming
body: Many delay the Stronghold and miss the Xesht invitation; finishing it first is the efficient move.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If your Breach keeps ending with almost no Splinters, you are likely on a closed map or moving too slow; switch to open layouts and a faster clear.
If Splinters will not combine, check you are holding the same Breachlord's Splinters; mixed Splinters do not form a Breachstone.
If the Xesht invitation never appears, you probably have not completed the Stronghold step; finish it before farming more Breachstones.
bullets: No Splinters = closed map or slow clear
